---

tl;dr: modular exponentiation with specific parameters is too slow and can introduce a DoS vector in specific cases.



The following is not really a general security issue but it can be harnessed as a DoS vector in some specific cases.



Ethereum allows users to upload virtual machine code which is subsequently run by other nodes on the network. Each type of operation inside the virtual machine is assigned a certain cost called gas, which roughly maps to the effective computation time of that operation, so that for any specific gas allotment, the upper bound on the total execution time of a virtual machine program (on a modern general purpose PC) can be estimated. Any program whose execution time far exceeds the expected upper bound for a specific gas allotment would be considered a bug by Ethereum.



One of the operations supported by the virtual machine is modular exponentiation with user-specified base, exponent and modulus. The gas cost is computed based on the size of these parameters, and always maps accurately to the computational cost of the modular exponentiation. However I found an exception to this, which is the following:
